metaData.originalTitle: 云原生 - AI Native 多智能体数字人架构实践
metaData.title: Cloud Native - AI Native Multi-Agent Digital Human Architecture Practice
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces Alibaba Cloud's AI Native multi-agent digital human collaboration platform, AgentTeams, built on cloud-native principles. It uses declarative CRDs to model organizational structures and collaboration strategies, enabling multiple agents to work together like a team, and shares practical implementations in R&D, on-call, and open-source maintenance scenarios.
metaData.summary: Starting with the scenario of automatic diagnosis of early morning alerts, the article highlights the necessity of multi-agent collaboration. The author traces the evolution from RPA to single agents and then to multi-agent collaboration, proposing that the core of AI Native is to 'design systems inherently around AI agents.' The core content revolves around AgentTeams: a collaboration orchestration and governance plane that uses four CRDs—Manager, Team, Worker, and Human—to declaratively model organizational structures, and designs a three-tier permission system (L1/L2/L3) to natively support HITL. The article details a deployment path based on cloud products, including security practices such as network connectivity and credential convergence to an AI gateway. Finally, it shares the real-world results of four AI Native scenarios (full-cycle R&D, intelligent on-call, open-source pipeline, business analysis), demonstrating capabilities such as a digital human team closing a ticket within 6 minutes and automatically analyzing issues and submitting PRs.

mainPoints.point: The core of AI Native is to design systems inherently around AI agents, rather than integrating AI capabilities as an add-on.
mainPoints.explanation: Analogous to Cloud Native enabling applications to be born on the cloud, AI Native treats agents as first-class citizens for declaration, orchestration, and governance, solving the three major problems of replicability, governability, and evolvability.

mainPoints.point: AgentTeams uses declarative CRDs to model organizational structures, enabling multiple agents to collaborate like a team.
mainPoints.explanation: Core resources include Manager (platform control), Team (department), Worker (employee), and Human (real person), with a collaboration chain of TeamAdmin → TeamLeader → Workers, and permission policies controlling who can talk to whom.

mainPoints.point: HITL (Human-in-the-Loop) is a first-class citizen in AgentTeams, not a patch.
mainPoints.explanation: The three-tier permission design (L1/L2/L3) of the Human CRD allows real people to naturally integrate into the agent collaboration process, intervening at key decision points to achieve human-machine co-governance.

mainPoints.point: Converging credentials to the AI gateway is a key security practice for production environments.
mainPoints.explanation: API keys for LLMs, MCP, and internal services are not scattered across agent containers but are held by the gateway. Workers only obtain revocable Consumer Tokens, and the gateway performs per-route authorization.

mainPoints.point: Real-world scenarios validate that multi-agent collaboration can compress a process that traditionally requires hours of coordination among multiple people into a minute-level conversation flow.
mainPoints.explanation: In the intelligent on-call scenario, three digital employees complete the full loop of 'receiving ticket → routing → root cause diagnosis → fix proposal → reply suggestion' within 6 minutes. In the open-source pipeline scenario, they automatically complete issue analysis, code generation, PR submission, and fixes.

keyQuotes: AgentTeams' official positioning is very clear: Collaboration Orchestration Plane. It does not replace the agent runtime, nor does it replace inference services or tool services. It focuses on one thing—making multiple agents operate like a real organization.

Over the past decade, cloud native has freed us from worrying about 'how applications run on servers,' making infrastructure like water and electricity. In the next decade, AI Native will free us from worrying about 'how AI works within the business.'

Multi-agent collaboration is not something that can be solved by writing scripts. It requires a control and governance plane like Kubernetes—declarative APIs, continuous reconciliation, clear resource boundaries, and governable permissions and communication.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: A Practical Guide to 'Progressive Spec' for AI Coding in 2026
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a 'Progressive Spec' framework for AI coding environments, leveraging structured documentation to drive AI collaboration and balance development standards with execution efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: The AI Native Era: Where Is R&D Organization Headed?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the paradigm shift of R&D organizations in the AI Native era, proposing that organizational structures will evolve from human-centric Org Charts to Execution Graphs that include both humans and AI Agents, and systematically analyzes core issues such as new bottlenecks, management collapse, and the governance of three types of work.

relatedArticles.title: From Toy to Productivity: Demystifying AI Agent Harness Engineering Through Real Projects
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the practical experience of the real-world project Aegis, this article systematically elaborates on the concept, architectural boundaries, and implementation methods of Harness Engineering. It argues that in enterprise engineering environments, constraining and governing non-deterministic large models by building a control plane is the key to transforming AI Agents from toys into productive tools, and it drives the migration of the engineer's role from code executor to goal controller.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces the concept of AI Agent Skill, including its directory structure, writing standards, release process, and cross-platform challenges. It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.
